input.question: Why are some many comets peanut-shaped?
input.ground_truth: That's what you get if two roughly spherical solid objects approach each other slowly and stick together. [Ultima Thule](_URL_1_) is a good example, you can clearly see the two components. For asteroids near Earth we have enough data for statistics: [10-15% are contact binaries](_URL_0_).

Okay! Imagine you have a big, soft snowball. If you squeeze it gently between your hands, what happens? It gets long and skinny in the middle, but stays round at the ends, kind of like a peanut!

Comets are a bit like that snowball in space. When they fly close to the Sun, the heat makes the middle melt a little faster than the sides. So, the middle gets smaller and the two ends stay bigger, making the comet look like a peanut!

So, comets become peanut-shaped because the middle melts more and makes them look like a peanut.
